newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-Wellington backs itself for Cup semi vs Canty.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Wellington backs itself for Cup semi vs Canty.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 7 - Wellington is backing its away-from-home record this season to dent Canterbury's receding aura of invincibility in Tuesday's Shell Cup semi-final in Christchurch, NZPA reports.
Wellington is unbeaten on the road this summer, with its only non-result being a washed-out game against Auckland.
Canterbury, which has dominated one-day game during the 1990s, has already lost to Wellington at Lancaster Park this summer.

It has also suffered defeats by Central Districts, which put on a stunning rearguard action at Napier, and at Auckland on Sunday after an all-out assault by Sri Lankan ace Aravinda de Silva, who hit 106 not out from 65 balls.
Wellington skipper Roger Twose is unfazed about making the trip south tomorrow.
"We've beaten every side in the competition this year, and we won at Lancaster Park on our last visit," he said.

"It is the business end of the season and I think it is good that the teams who have finished first and second in the round-robin side of the draw will play the semi-final... I think we will play the final as well," he said.

Twose, who watched Richard Petrie and Glenn Jonas fail to close the door on Northern Districts' fighting ninth wicket partnership which won them yesterday's game by two wickets, was confident that the bowling would recover for tomorrow's semi-final. "I still think we can win the Shell Cup," he said.
In the first round of the Cup Wellington was rolled out for 66, its record low score in one-day play, by Canterbury. But then in the second round it beat Canterbury with a score of 209-8.
Some outstanding semi-finals and finals have been played between the two teams, with the 1992 final still regarded as one of the greatest one-day games played in New Zealand.

Two summers ago, Wellington secured a 10-wicket semi-final win over Canterbury when John Aiken and Mark Douglas combined in an unbroken 205-run opening stand, only to then be beaten in the final by Northern Districts.
Because Scott Weenink suffered a thigh injury yesterday when batting, his place in Christchurch could be taken by Scott McHardy at the top of the Wellington order.
